summary: In this story, an old fisherman teaches his grandson that patience and reading the water matter more than having an expensive net.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Clever Fisherman's Net” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: the steady movement of water in one direction
a small wave or circle that moves across the surface of water
a particular way of doing something that takes skill

challengeTerms.def: a custom or way of doing something that is passed down over many years
good at noticing small details that other people often miss
to expect or sense that something is going to happen before it does

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that having better equipment is the most important part of being good at something? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain why Saleh was able to catch a fish when Yusuf could not.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review current, ripple, and technique, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tradition, observant, and anticipate to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
